title: Beef Pho
subtitle: Vietnamese beef noodle soup
excerpt: A rich, spiced beef broth with rice noodles and paper-thin slices of beef. The broth takes time but the method is simple and the result is deeply satisfying.
sourceNotes: Synthesised from classic Vietnamese pho recipes. Charring the onion and ginger before simmering is standard practice across all major sources.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze the broth only. Cool fully and freeze for up to 3 months. Cook fresh noodles and beef when serving.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: The broth can be made up to 3 days ahead and kept in the fridge.

content.text: Charring the onion and ginger gives the broth its smoky depth. Keep the heat low once the beef shin goes in so the broth stays clear.

items.prepNote: sliced paper-thin, to serve raw in bowls
soaked in cold water for 30 minutes, then drained

content.text: Heat the grill to high. Place the onion halves and ginger cut-side up on a baking tray. Grill for 8 to 10 minutes until charred and softened.
Put the beef shin in the stockpot. Cover with cold water and bring to the boil. Boil for 2 minutes, then drain. Rinse the beef and the pot well.
Return the beef shin to the pot. Add the charred onion and ginger. Add the star-anise, cloves, cinnamon, fish sauce, and palm sugar.
Pour in the beef stock and top up with 500ml cold water. Bring to a gentle simmer over medium heat.
Simmer on very low heat for 1 hour 30 minutes. Skim any foam from the surface every 30 minutes.
Lift out the beef shin. Shred it into pieces and set aside. Strain the broth through a sieve. Discard the solids. Taste the broth and add more fish sauce if needed.
Cook the soaked rice noodles in boiling water for 2 to 3 minutes. Drain and divide between four bowls.
Top the noodles with shredded beef shin and a few slices of raw sirloin. Bring the broth back to a rolling boil.
Ladle the very hot broth over the raw sirloin. The heat of the broth cooks the beef in the bowl. Top with spring onion, coriander, chilli, and a wedge of lime.

items.cause: It was boiled too hard after the initial blanch.
items.fix: Keep heat very low; a gentle simmer, not a boil.

items.cause: Not enough fish sauce or palm sugar to balance.
items.fix: Add fish sauce in small splashes and taste after each.

items.symptom: Raw sirloin still pink after pouring broth.
items.cause: Broth was not hot enough when ladled.
items.fix: Make sure broth is at a full rolling boil before ladling.
